newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian lending rate falls to 10.8 from 11.1 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatian lending rate falls to 10.8 from 11.1 pct.

text.p: The Croatian average money market rate edged down 30 basis points to 10.8 percent amid good banking liquidity, delears said.
Daily settlements were 30.5 million kuna, against 55.5 million on offer.
Dealers said fresh loans accounted for 20 million kuna, most of which were call money placements struck at an unchanged 10.5 percent rate.
One 30-day interbank deal was made at a regular 15 percent and savings banks were granted one-month funds at 15 and 16 percent.
Insurers rolled over previous loans at nine percent. Banks prolonged one-week funds at 11.5 percent.
The central bank calculated its kuna midrates for Wednesday weaker ar 6.1062 versus the dollar and slightly firmer at 3.5742 against the German mark. -- Laura Lui, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
